<!--
  THE DASHBOARD FIGURE — entanglement figure slide 2, redrawn at site scale.

  IT OPENS ACT 2, right after the gif returns, and that placement is the point:
  figure 2 was three slides ago, so the echo is still in the room's head. It
  used to sit in Act 5, ~28 slides later, where the callback had decayed to the
  point of needing reconstruction. Moving it here also resolved a duplication —
  Act 5's `It looks like an application. It isn't.` says the same thing in
  bullets, and now reads as the recap of this rather than a second first pass.
  The move cost the map feeder, which had to go: see the note where it used to
  be. Two clicks now, not three.

  It is a CALLBACK, not a new picture. The left half is byte-identical to figure
  2's opened state — me at 200, agent at 400, the same 110x64 and 180x64 boxes,
  the same dashed agent, the same 80-unit arrows, the same `writes` label at
  y=161 — and the .qmd's front card is figure 2's .qmd box at its exact
  coordinates (670,113,190,124) with the same teal `yaml` and yellow `content`
  bands inside it. Everything the room already learned is free; only the two
  ends changed.

  THE viewBox IS "185 68 935 342". Coordinates inside are figure 2's, so every
  box sits at the same place in the drawing and the callback survives; what
  differs is the CROP. It is tuned to the real ink (x 200..1104, y 74..400): at
  553 tall — the height figure 2 used to carry — this figure had ~200 units of
  dead canvas and was HEIGHT-bound, so it rendered small and floated high with
  wide side gaps. At 342 the aspect is 2.7 against the frame's ~2.2, so it is
  WIDTH-bound and fills the slide. That is the whole reason the boxes read
  bigger here, and it is the same fix figure 2 has now had. y=68 is what stops
  `.qmd x 15` from being clipped: a 22px baseline at y=90 has its ascender
  near 74. Restoring the map feeder would push the ink to y=422 and the height
  back to 364.

  ⚠️ The width is 935, not 895, and the 40 units are the price of CENTRING
  `vehicletrends.us` on the window: the label is ~192 units wide against a
  115-wide window, so it overhangs to x=1104. That costs ~4% of scale — the
  whole figure renders slightly smaller so the label can sit where it belongs.
  Shrinking the label's font is the lever if that trade ever stops being worth
  it; anchoring it `end` again is not, since that is the bug this fixed.

  WHAT CHANGED, and it is the whole slide:
    * one .qmd became a STACK of them, and the agent's arrow still lands on ONE
      card. That is the small-context claim, drawn rather than asserted.
    * the .pdf page became a BROWSER WINDOW. This is the deck's one departure
      from "the artifact is a page with a folded corner" and it is deliberate:
      the artifact here is a site, and the window is what makes `It's not an
      app, it's a website` visible. Its content area still carries the
      interleaved teal/yellow bands, because a rendered artifact is still
      entangled — that never was the problem.
    * two feeders arrive on click. Both point INTO the chain from outside, which
      is the composition claim: the data and the heavy component are things the
      page refers to, not things the agent wrote.

  THE STACK IS FLUSH RIGHT AT x=860 and fans left-and-up (686/678/670, tops
  97/105/113, widths 174/182/190). That is not decoration — it is what keeps the
  `render` arrow at figure 2's exact 862..942. Offset the cards the usual
  down-right way and the back card collides with the arrow, and the whole right
  half has to be renumbered. Back cards are drawn FIRST so the front covers
  them; each shows as an 8-unit strip along its top edge.

  Yellow appears only as the data box's FILL and the content band's, never as a
  line or a letter — the palette rule. Text on yellow is navy.

  Marker id `ahDash` is unique document-wide; reveal display:none's non-current
  slides, so ids may not be shared across them.

  VETTED ONCE (2026-08-15) and fixed: the stack reads as sheets, the browser
  reads as a browser, `vehicletrends.us` clears the right edge. Three things
  were wrong and are corrected above — the clipped top label, ~200px of dead
  canvas, and click 1's arrow drawn straight through a caption centred on the
  stack. Still unvetted: the re-cropped viewBox, and the caption in its new
  place under the agent.
-->

```{=html}
<svg viewBox="185 68 935 342" width="100%" style="max-height:85vh;"
     xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     font-family="'Fira Sans Condensed', Tahoma, sans-serif">

  <defs>
    <marker id="ahDash" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="5.5" refY="3"
            orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3 L0,6 z" fill="#2e4057"/></marker>
    <marker id="ahEditDash" markerWidth="9" markerHeight="9" refX="5.5" refY="3"
            orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L7,3 L0,6 z" fill="#852f88"/></marker>
  </defs>

  <!-- ── AT REST: I asked for the website ─────────────────────────────────
       me -> agent -> the site, one arrow, no source anywhere. This is figure
       slide 1's claim wearing a dashboard: I asked for the artifact and the
       agent handed me the artifact.

       CLICK 1 opens the chain and drops the fifteen .qmd into the gap — the
       identical mechanism figure 2 uses, down to the same ±140. That is not a
       coincidence and it is worth checking if these coordinates ever change:
       closed, the agent's right edge is 580+140=720 and the site's left is
       950-140=810, leaving 90 = 2 gap + 80 arrow + 8 landing. Solve
       370-2s = 90 and s is 140. Both shifts are CSS transforms on
       `fragment custom` groups (`.openleft` / `.openright` in custom.css);
       reveal's `:not(.custom)` rule leaves them visible at rest and only
       toggles `.visible`. ⚠️ If that CSS is ever lost the boxes simply stay
       closed and the stack lands on top of the site — these two rules are NOT
       optional. -->

  <g class="fragment custom openleft" data-fragment-index="1">
    <rect x="340" y="143" width="110" height="64" rx="6"
          fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <text x="395" y="184" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2e4057">me</text>

    <path d="M 452 175 L 532 175" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"
          marker-end="url(#ahDash)"/>

    <!-- Still dashed. Nothing about the agent improved between figure 2 and
         here; what improved is the shape of what it writes into. -->
    <rect x="540" y="143" width="180" height="64" rx="6"
          fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"
          stroke-dasharray="7 5"/>
    <text x="630" y="184" font-size="24" text-anchor="middle" fill="#2e4057">LLM agent</text>

    <!-- The direct agent -> site arrow: "make me a dashboard," and out comes a
         dashboard. It rides along with the agent as the chain opens and fades
         as the .qmd take its place — nested here on purpose so it stays
         attached to the agent while it goes. Same move as figure 2. -->
    <g class="fragment fade-out" data-fragment-index="1">
      <path d="M 722 175 L 802 175" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"
            marker-end="url(#ahDash)"/>
    </g>
  </g>

  <!-- ❌ NOTHING goes above the agent. A caption there ("one page in context",
       "opens one page at a time") was tried and cut: the arrow already lands on
       exactly one card, which says it without a line of type, and the claim is
       John's to make out loud. Under the stack and under the agent are both
       occupied anyway — by click 2's feeder and by the purple fork. -->

  <!-- ── CLICK 1: the stack arrives. Back cards first, flush right at 860. ──
       Drawn at OPENED coordinates and never moved — it is the thing the gap
       opens for, so it fades in where it belongs rather than gliding. -->
  <g class="fragment" data-fragment-index="1">
    <text x="622" y="161" font-size="20" fill="#2e4057"
          text-anchor="middle">writes</text>
    <path d="M 582 175 L 662 175" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"
          marker-end="url(#ahDash)"/>

    <text x="765" y="90" font-size="22" text-anchor="middle"
          fill="#2e4057" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">.qmd &#215; 15</text>

    <rect x="686" y="97" width="174" height="124" rx="6"
          fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <rect x="678" y="105" width="182" height="124" rx="6"
          fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>

    <!-- The front card IS figure 2's .qmd — same box, same two bands, same
         coordinates. The arrow lands here and only here. -->
    <rect x="670" y="113" width="190" height="124" rx="6"
          fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <rect x="686" y="129" width="158" height="36" fill="#00798c"/>
    <text x="765" y="154" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle"
          fill="#FFFFFF" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">yaml</text>
    <rect x="686" y="177" width="158" height="44" fill="#edae49"/>
    <text x="765" y="206" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle"
          fill="#2e4057" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">content</text>

    <text x="902" y="161" font-size="20" fill="#2e4057"
          text-anchor="middle">render</text>
    <path d="M 862 175 L 942 175" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"
          marker-end="url(#ahDash)"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ── The site. Glides RIGHT as the chain opens. ─────────────────────────
       Drawn 140 left of its opened home, so every x here is (opened - 140):
       the window at 810 lands at 950, and the label's centre 867.5 lands at
       1007.5, which is the window's own centre. ⚠️ The label is `text-anchor
       middle` on the WINDOW's centre, not `end` on its right edge — it used to
       be the latter and hung visibly off to the right. That centring is what
       sets the viewBox width: "vehicletrends.us" is 16 mono characters at 20px,
       so ~192 units wide, and it overhangs the 115-wide window by ~38 units on
       each side. -->
  <g class="fragment custom openright" data-fragment-index="1">
    <text x="867" y="98" font-size="20" text-anchor="middle"
          fill="#2e4057" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">vehicletrends.us</text>

    <rect x="810" y="110" width="115" height="130" rx="6"
          fill="#FFFFFF" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <path d="M 810 132 L 925 132" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2"/>
    <circle cx="822" cy="121" r="3" fill="#2e4057"/>
    <circle cx="833" cy="121" r="3" fill="#2e4057"/>
    <circle cx="844" cy="121" r="3" fill="#2e4057"/>

    <!-- The sidebar is the navigation Quarto wrote, not the agent. -->
    <path d="M 844 132 L 844 240" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2"/>
    <rect x="816" y="144" width="20" height="5" fill="#2e4057"/>
    <rect x="816" y="157" width="20" height="5" fill="#2e4057"/>
    <rect x="816" y="170" width="20" height="5" fill="#2e4057"/>
    <rect x="816" y="183" width="20" height="5" fill="#2e4057"/>

    <!-- Still interleaved. The OUTPUT was never the thing that had to change. -->
    <rect x="852" y="140" width="64" height="10" fill="#00798c"/>
    <rect x="852" y="154" width="64" height="14" fill="#edae49"/>
    <rect x="852" y="172" width="64" height="8"  fill="#00798c"/>
    <rect x="852" y="184" width="64" height="16" fill="#edae49"/>
    <rect x="852" y="204" width="64" height="10" fill="#00798c"/>
    <rect x="852" y="218" width="64" height="8"  fill="#edae49"/>
  </g>

  <!-- ── CLICK 2: the data comes from outside, at render ───────────────── -->
  <!-- `library(vehicletrends)` executing during `quarto render`: the data flows
       through the code and the numbers are baked into the output. It lands on
       the STACK because that is literally where it goes. -->
  <g class="fragment" data-fragment-index="2">
    <path d="M 765 330 L 765 250" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"
          marker-end="url(#ahDash)"/>
    <rect x="670" y="332" width="190" height="64" rx="6"
          fill="#edae49" stroke="#2e4057" stroke-width="2.5"/>
    <text x="765" y="356" font-size="19" text-anchor="middle"
          fill="#2e4057" font-family="SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace">{vehicletrends}</text>
    <text x="765" y="380" font-size="18" text-anchor="middle"
          fill="#2e4057">R data package</text>
  </g>

  <!-- ❌ NO MAP FEEDER. A second box hung under the browser — an arrow up into
       the site, `<iframe>` / map / `</iframe>` — was drawn and cut once this
       figure moved to open Act 2: the `Put it in a box` slides are still ahead
       of it here, so the box previewed rather than recalled, and the figure had
       to be talked around instead of read. The box slides make the point on
       their own. Restoring it costs a fragment index, a taller box (90 not 64,
       to hold three lines, top at y=332 to stay level with the data box), and
       ~20 units of viewBox height.

       If it ever comes back: ❌ its arrow must point at the BROWSER, never at
       the stack. The .qmd holds six lines that emit `<iframe src=...>`; the
       render copies that URL and stops. The 276 lines of MapLibre and the
       1.64 GB of tiles are fetched from another origin by the READER's browser,
       so the map never enters the .qmd, the render, or the built site. -->

  <!-- ── CLICK 3: and I can still reach in ─────────────────────────────── -->
  <!-- Figure 2's forked purple descent, unchanged and on purpose: same x=255
       origin out of `me`, same rails at y=263 and y=309, same landings 8 units
       under the agent (490,215) and under the .qmd (690,245). The front card is
       at figure 2's coordinates, so the lower arrow's landing point needed no
       recomputing at all — which is the payoff for keeping the box where it was.

       It comes LAST here, not second as it does in figure 2. There the fork is
       the answer to "the content now has an address"; here it is the answer to
       everything already on screen — fifteen pages and a data package feeding
       them, and I can still change any of it. Purple is still YOUR action, and
       both branches are yours: delegating the typing to the agent is a choice
       you make.

       It is OUTSIDE `.openleft`, at `me`'s opened x=255, because it only ever
       appears after the chain has opened. The rails clear everything: the upper
       spans x 267..478, the lower 267..678, and click 2's feeder comes up at
       x=765, right of both. -->
  <g class="fragment" data-fragment-index="3">
    <path d="M 255 211 L 255 251 Q 255 263 267 263 L 478 263 Q 490 263 490 251 L 490 215"
          fill="none" stroke="#852f88" stroke-width="2.5"
          marker-end="url(#ahEditDash)"/>
    <text x="420" y="285" font-size="20" fill="#852f88"
          text-anchor="middle">prompt the agent to edit a .qmd...</text>

    <path d="M 255 263 L 255 297 Q 255 309 267 309 L 678 309 Q 690 309 690 297 L 690 245"
          fill="none" stroke="#852f88" stroke-width="2.5"
          marker-end="url(#ahEditDash)"/>
    <text x="472" y="335" font-size="20" fill="#852f88"
          text-anchor="middle">…or edit it directly</text>
  </g>

</svg>
```
